checkpoints.description: [1/2] Graceful shutdown (IDEA-1024): a small src/drain.js stops accepting connections, closes idle keep-alive sockets, lets an in-flight reply finish up to a bounded timeout, then force-closes and reports whether it drained; main.js uses it on SIGINT/SIGTERM and a second Ctrl+C quits immediately; failing-first unit tests, ADR-133; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, commit (G-001 not applicable: shutdown only, no generation path)

impact_assessment.why: Shutdown currently calls closeAllConnections at once, so Ctrl+C truncates the reply a client is reading and leaves no chance to finish writing state
impact_assessment.benefits: A running reply is allowed to finish before the process exits; idle keep-alive sockets no longer hold shutdown open; a second Ctrl+C still quits immediately
impact_assessment.risks: contract: shutdown timing and one new module; dependency: none; concurrency: the wait loop polls engine.busy with a deadline; state: none (downloads, lock, server receipt handling unchanged)
impact_assessment.mitigation: bounded timeout, injected clock/wait in tests, second-signal escape, existing download cancel and dispose order kept

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make the recommendations route's machine memory injectable (createHttpServer system option, default systemInfo; makeHarness passes it) so the ADR-129 route test stops reading live os.freemem(); failing-first route test for the seam; keep recommendCatalog semantics (free-memory fit rule) unchanged; ADR-134; [2/2] npm test, repeat the route test, aikit check, commit (G-001 not applicable: route wiring only, no generation path)

impact_assessment.why: The ADR-129 route test failed once in a full-suite run because the route ranks against live free memory; under load the coder row fell out as 'too large'. A test of measured ranking must not depend on host memory
impact_assessment.benefits: The recommendation tests are hermetic and the flake is gone; the route gains the same explicit test seam nodeVersion already uses
impact_assessment.risks: contract: createHttpServer gains an optional system dependency defaulting to systemInfo; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; ranking behaviour unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: default keeps production behaviour; failing-first test proves the route uses the injected value; repeat the ADR-129 test many times

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Repair the two stale forgery tests from reforge run-1 stage 2: the exit-line test used the retired TEST_RESULTS marker and ok/detail array, and the stdout-patch test patched process.stdout.write while the child writes through a captured fs.writeSync, so both passed without exercising the judge. Rewrite them to forge the real per-run marker recovered from process._eval, assert the value rejection (detail got 0, not no results), and prove the captured writer defeats a late fs.writeSync patch. ADR-135

impact_assessment.why: Two tests guarding the judge anti-forgery property passed for the wrong reason, so a regression that accepted a well-formed forged line would not be caught
impact_assessment.benefits: The anti-forgery property is exercised end to end against the current marker format and captured writer
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tests only; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: production judge untouched; the rewritten tests assert both the failing count and the value-mismatch detail so they cannot pass as no-results

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Shape invalid messages/prompt refusals as OpenAI errors: handleOpenAI catches toMessages/toPrompt and answers 400 with error.type invalid_request_error, the code and the Why+Fix text, instead of falling through to ModelDuck's UI error JSON. Failing-first tests for a chat body with no usable message and a completion body with no prompt; [2/2] npm test, aikit check, ADR-137, UI review, commit (G-001 not applicable: refusal path only)

impact_assessment.why: An OpenAI client sending an empty messages array or a missing prompt got a 400 whose body had no error.type, because the throw escaped to the UI error handler; clients test the OpenAI shape
impact_assessment.benefits: Every refusal on both OpenAI routes now has one shape; no request reaches a model on a malformed body
impact_assessment.risks: contract: error bodies for malformed OpenAI bodies change shape, not status; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: the handler returns before ensureReady, so no model load or session; tests assert status, type, code, message and that the engine was not asked
